title: Pruvz Public Evidence Packet — action record
description: One recorded business action as the Pruvz product API reports it (the action details view, GET /api/actions/{actionId}): the action's business identity, its two separate state machines (execution and verification), the embedded immutable decision-time Policy Snapshot, the frozen verification timing resolved at acceptance (format 1.1.0), the human review lifecycle of a terminal non-verified result (format 1.2.0), the human-triggered re-verification after a RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY review event (format 1.3.0: the fresh re-verification window and the independently-confirmed marker), the exact decimal representation every money value carries for cryptographic commitment (format 1.4.0), and the three deliberately separated value groups a reviewer compares — the server-derived expected outcome, the agent's unverified claim, and what independent system-of-record read-back actually observed.

actionId.description: Server-generated identifier of the business action.

agentId.description: The agent that requested the action.

runId.description: The demo/agent run this action belongs to.

correlationId.description: The business correlation key, e.g. the payment the refund belongs to.

actionType.description: The kind of business action, e.g. "refund".

crmTicketId.description: The CRM ticket the decision context referenced; null when none was asserted.

claim.description: The agent's unverified claim about its own execution outcome; null until a claim is recorded. A claim never decides the verification result.

expectedOutcome.description: Derived by Pruvz server-side from the decision and the immutable Policy Snapshot — never accepted as an agent input. Null until derived.

observed.description: What independent system-of-record read-back actually observed: the latest INDEPENDENT_READBACK evidence, summarized. Null means no independent observation was recorded yet — reported honestly instead of echoing the claim or the expectation.

executionStatus.description: Agent execution progress — what the agent reports. Separate from verificationStatus by design.

verificationStatus.description: Independent verification state — what Pruvz proved. Terminal results (VERIFIED, OUTCOME_MISMATCH, VERIFICATION_FAILED) are assigned only after independent system-of-record read-back, never through any agent-facing contract.

finalOutcome.description: The proven business outcome, e.g. REFUND_SUCCEEDED. Present exactly when verificationStatus is VERIFIED; a mismatch or a technical failure never fabricates one.

verificationFailure.description: Why verification failed. Present exactly when verificationStatus is VERIFICATION_FAILED: a technical description of an unreadable source, never a business result.

reviewState.description: Where the action stands in the human review lifecycle (format 1.2.0 widened the vocabulary). Only a terminal verification result determines it: NOT_DETERMINED until verification concludes; NOT_REQUIRED for a first-pass VERIFIED, which auto-clears and never enters review; for an OUTCOME_MISMATCH or VERIFICATION_FAILED result, the workflow state — PENDING_REVIEW (awaiting a human decision), NEEDS_CORRECTION (a correction outside Pruvz is required), AWAITING_REVERIFICATION (the correction was reported and control returned to Pruvz for an independent re-verification) or DECIDED (closed by a terminal human disposition); and, since format 1.3.0, DECIDED on a VERIFIED action whose review was closed because Pruvz's re-verification independently confirmed the externally-reported resolution.

review.description: The human review of a terminal non-verified result (format 1.2.0): its category, the current disposition and the complete decision history. Present when verificationStatus is OUTCOME_MISMATCH or VERIFICATION_FAILED — and, since format 1.3.0, on a VERIFIED action whose review was closed because an independent re-verification confirmed the externally-reported resolution (independentlyConfirmed true); null otherwise. A human decision is appended as HUMAN_REVIEW_DECISION evidence and never rewrites the verification result: no review decision can produce VERIFIED — only Pruvz's own re-verification can.

mismatch.description: The expected-versus-observed dimensions behind an OUTCOME_MISMATCH ruling. Present exactly when verificationStatus is OUTCOME_MISMATCH; a technical failure never carries one.

verificationTiming.description: The action's frozen verification timing (format 1.1.0): resolved exactly once when the action was accepted and never re-resolved, so later policy or configuration changes cannot affect an in-flight action. deadlineAtUtc null means no verification deadline was resolved — such an action can never produce a time-based mismatch and is reported as "verification deadline not configured". Null only on action records that predate the timing model.

reverificationTiming.description: The fresh verification window of the latest human-triggered re-verification (format 1.3.0): resolved through the same precedence chain as verificationTiming, but anchored to the moment the external correction was reported (the RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY review event), because the original deadline had already passed when the action mismatched. Null while no RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY event ever triggered a re-verification; it never replaces verificationTiming, which stays the immutable record of the original window.

verificationCompletedAtUtc.description: When the terminal verification result was assigned; null while verification has not concluded.

allOf.$comment: VERIFIED carries the proven outcome and never a failure or mismatch block. A first-pass VERIFIED auto-clears (no review). Since format 1.3.0 a VERIFIED action may instead carry a DECIDED review with independentlyConfirmed true: the action mismatched or failed, a human reported the correction (RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY), and Pruvz's own re-verification — inside the fresh window recorded in reverificationTiming — independently confirmed the resolution.
OUTCOME_MISMATCH carries its mismatch dimensions and is under review as a business exception (category BUSINESS_MISMATCH); nothing was proven, so no final outcome and no failure block.

VERIFICATION_FAILED is a technical outcome: it carries the failure block and never a business result or a mismatch story. Since format 1.2.0 an exhausted failure is under review in its own category (VERIFICATION_FAILURE) — 'verification could not be completed' — distinct from a business mismatch.
Before verification concludes nothing terminal may appear: no outcome, no failure, no mismatch, no review, no completion time, and the need for review is honestly undetermined.
AWAITING_REVERIFICATION means a RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY event returned control to Pruvz for an independent re-check (format 1.3.0) — the fresh window that governs it must be recorded.

utcTimestamp.description: A UTC timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with the Z (Zulu) UTC designator, matching the *AtUtc field names. Local-offset forms such as +03:00 are not valid in this contract.

money.description: An amount of money in a single ISO 4217 currency, in two representations of the same value: amount, the JSON number consumers display, and amountExact (format 1.4.0), the exact canonical decimal string. Cryptographic commitments bind to amountExact and never to the number, because a JSON number read through IEEE-754 double semantics cannot be reproduced exactly by every runtime. The two must agree; a packet whose representations disagree is rejected by the bundled validator's consistency layer.

amountExact.description: The exact amount in canonical decimal form, so that one value has exactly one spelling: no exponent, no plus sign, no leading zeros (zero is a bare 0) and no trailing zeros in the fraction — 25.00 is written 25 and 25.50 is written 25.5. The digit bounds admit every value the product's exact decimal type can hold, so a producible amount can never be unexpressible here.

subject.description: The business entity the action operates on.

decision.description: What the policy evaluation approved. Its amount is the decision amount, never a verified amount.

observed.description: The latest independent read-back observation, summarized. Field names match the evidence timeline items so this block can be correlated with its timeline entry.

verificationTiming.description: The frozen verification timing (format 1.1.0): the technical clock (when the first read-back is meaningful, how often absence is re-checked) and the business clock (the resolved verification deadline with its provenance). Spans are integer seconds so consumers never parse a duration format.

deadlineAtUtc.description: When the business window closes; null when no deadline was resolved — absence then never becomes a time-based mismatch.

deadlineSource.description: Where the deadline came from, in resolution precedence order: POLICY (the decision-time Policy Snapshot), TENANT_OVERRIDE (explicit tenant/action configuration), PRODUCT_SPEC (the product's per-action-type default — which may also be an explicit no-deadline decision), or NOT_CONFIGURED (no source resolved a deadline).

resolvedAtUtc.description: The acceptance moment the resolution was made and the deadline anchored to.

allOf.$comment: A POLICY or TENANT_OVERRIDE provenance always carries a concrete deadline.
NOT_CONFIGURED means no source resolved a deadline, so none may appear.

reviewWorkflowState.description: The review states an action under review can be in (format 1.2.0). The locked human transitions: PENDING_REVIEW + APPROVED_EXCEPTION or DISMISSED → DECIDED; PENDING_REVIEW + NEEDS_CORRECTION → NEEDS_CORRECTION; PENDING_REVIEW or NEEDS_CORRECTION + RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY → AWAITING_REVERIFICATION; NEEDS_CORRECTION + DISMISSED → DECIDED. DECIDED is closed; AWAITING_REVERIFICATION accepts no human decision until Pruvz re-verifies. Since format 1.3.0 the re-verification itself moves the review — a Worker transition that appends no decision entry: a re-verification that confirms the resolution (VERIFIED) closes the review as DECIDED, and one that rules OUTCOME_MISMATCH or exhausts as VERIFICATION_FAILED returns the review to PENDING_REVIEW under the category of the new result.

review.description: The human review of one terminal non-verified result (format 1.2.0): the category that opened it, the current disposition, and the complete decision history as recorded on the append-only evidence timeline. Since format 1.3.0 it also states whether an independent re-verification confirmed an externally-reported resolution.

category.description: Why the action is under review, derived from the terminal result and never chosen: BUSINESS_MISMATCH (an OUTCOME_MISMATCH — a definitive business exception requiring a business decision) or VERIFICATION_FAILURE (a VERIFICATION_FAILED after technical retry exhaustion — verification could not be completed; there is no business exception to approve). On a VERIFIED action whose review was closed by a confirming re-verification (format 1.3.0), the category of the superseded result that had opened the review.

independentlyConfirmed.description: True exactly when Pruvz's own re-verification — not the human report — confirmed the externally-reported resolution and closed the review (format 1.3.0): the action is VERIFIED and DECIDED, and the distinction from a human-resolved disposition (APPROVED_EXCEPTION or DISMISSED, where independentlyConfirmed stays false) is the packet's human-resolved versus independently-confirmed-resolved line.

latestDecision.description: The current disposition: the most recent human decision or event recorded on this review, or null while none was recorded.

decisions.description: Every human decision and event recorded on this review, oldest first — one entry per HUMAN_REVIEW_DECISION item on the evidence timeline.

reviewDecision.description: One recorded human decision or event (format 1.2.0): what was decided, by whom and why, the review transition it caused, the evidence the reviewer ruled on, and where its attestation sits on the evidence timeline.

decision.description: APPROVED_EXCEPTION (terminal: the mismatch is accepted as an approved business exception; BUSINESS_MISMATCH only), DISMISSED (terminal: no remediation is required under business policy — it never means the machine result was wrong), NEEDS_CORRECTION (a correction outside Pruvz is required) or RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY (an event: the correction was made outside Pruvz; control returns to Pruvz for an independent re-verification).

reviewerId.description: The authenticated identity of the reviewer who decided.

reviewedEvidenceId.description: The evidence item the reviewer ruled on (the latest review-relevant item when the decision was made); at least one of id and sequence is present.

evidenceId.description: The HUMAN_REVIEW_DECISION item on the evidence timeline that records this decision.

businessDiscrepancy.description: The monetary business discrepancy of one mismatch, or its explicit absence: when evaluable is false there is no amount at all — an unknown discrepancy is never rendered as a zero, because "no amount" and "zero amount" are different business statements.

mismatch.description: The review classification and expected-versus-observed dimensions behind one OUTCOME_MISMATCH ruling. The observed side is stated as recorded business facts (refund counts, ticket statuses), never as source payload contents.

mismatchReason.description: The temporal mismatch category (format 1.1.0): CONTRADICTORY_EVIDENCE means positive evidence contradicts the claim, assigned immediately with no deadline wait; EXPECTED_OUTCOME_ABSENT_AFTER_DEADLINE means the expected outcome never appeared and the resolved verification deadline passed — only ever assigned when an explicit deadline was resolved. Derived from reasonCode server-side; the two can never disagree.

reasonCode.description: A stable machine classification code. Intentionally an open string: consumers must treat unknown future codes as valid and fall back to the explanation. Known v1.1.0 codes: NO_QUALIFYING_REFUND, MULTIPLE_QUALIFYING_REFUNDS, CRM_STATE_INCONSISTENT, REFUND_FAILED.

policySnapshot.description: The complete immutable decision-time Policy Snapshot embedded with the action: policy identity, the rules that applied, the normalized inputs the evaluation saw, and the explainable per-rule results. Read from stored state; never re-evaluated on read.

verificationDeadlineSeconds.description: The policy's verification deadline in seconds from action acceptance (format 1.1.0), or null when this policy version sets none. When set, it is the highest-precedence deadline source of the action's frozen verification timing (deadlineSource POLICY).

policyInput.description: The normalized inputs the decision-time evaluation saw.

policyEvaluation.description: The explainable decision-time result: overall pass plus one result per rule, in policy order.
